blocks.text: ERA ZERO CORE STANDARD 1.0.0 — COMPLETE 324-ROOT CATALOGUE

This section completes the canonical address inventory while preserving the Phase 1 authority boundary. The 36 source-approved LIF:000–222 and MOV:000–022 meanings above remain unchanged. The 288 Phase 2 meanings below were semantically audited, explicitly authorized by the user, and canonized in Era Zero Core Standard 1.0.0.
Core Standard 1.0.0 status and reading rules
Inventory: 324 total addresses = 324 canonical meanings, 0 provisional meanings, and 0 missing roots.
Review history: the 288 Phase 2 roots were organized into 32 ordered nine-root chunks; all 32 passed semantic audit and were approved together for Core Standard 1.0.0.
Encoding authority: family onset, harmonic signature, universal slot, compact root, family-qualified transliteration, formal carrier, and note path are generated from accepted algorithms.

Semantic authority: 36 meanings remain source-extracted; 288 meanings are audited design completions canonized by direct user authorization. Their provenance remains distinct in the machine-readable lexicon.
State separation: the third address trit is permanently lexical. A separate runtime ending [0], [1], or [2]/num states whether that lexical concept is currently inactive, active, or pending.
Runtime glosses: [0] inactive, false, ended, unavailable, or inaccessible; [1] active, valid, expressed, or executing; [2]/num dormant, pending, remembered, possible, or unresolved.
Canonical ORI / num resolution

ORI:002 is canonically nu·nan, “latent first condition,” under the latest compact-root algorithm. The word num is canonically reserved as the name of runtime state 2 and is not an alternate atomic form for ORI:002 in version 1.0.0. Possible historical contraction use remains deferred to the etymology layer.
